capabilities: Index task IDs from checkbox lines with 🆔 and ⛔ fields and report duplicate groups
Flag missing dependency targets, self-references, and ambiguous targets
Detect dependency cycles and list the IDs and source locations in each loop
Filter an audit to a vault folder and open a source line from the report
Save project profiles and report snapshots and re-run audits after file changes (Pro)
disambiguation: It only reports issues; the report does not repair dependencies or generate IDs.
extras: Freemium: core audit features are free; Pro (profiles, saved reports, repeat after file changes) requires a GitHub Sponsors sponsorship. After sign-in it contacts GitHub to verify sponsorship; before sign-in it makes no network requests and sends no vault data. After updates it opens a What's new tab promoting other NoteMods plugins and Zovo Chat. The README lists untested areas (phones, tablets, third-party sync conflicts, live payment transactions, Linux and Windows locally).
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to verify that task IDs are unique and that dependency references between tasks across notes actually resolve without loops.

relations.evidence: The Tasks plugin is not required to run the audit.

requires.name: GitHub Sponsors sponsorship of theluckystrike ($5/month or $15 once)

summary: Audit tool that scans Markdown task lines with 🆔 and ⛔ fields to find duplicate IDs, missing dependency targets, self-references, and dependency cycles.
